doc.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Recording on ECM with Steve Kuhn and Steve Swallow
summary: She recounts recording with Steve Kuhn's group and on Swallow's Robert Creeley setting Home.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Don Cherry. Uh, well, you there was a long association that helped bring your name to maybe a second generation after the sixties into the late seventies, early eighties when you teamed up with Harvey, Harvey S. Talk a little bit, little bit about that, that, how that came to be.

Yeah. I‟m not gonna go into detail about that because, you know, we talked about it a little bit off-camera. So I‟m just gonna say that, uh, I… for some reason, I got hooked on the bass a long time ago. I heard it. Now maybe in another life I was a bass player. I don‟t know. But I loved the bass. I love singing with the bass. And I used to sing with Swallow every chance I got at the Page Three to try out some things. Of course, the piano player would get all bent out of shape. But uh, I was with Steve Kuhn‟s group. I recorded several things on ECM with Steve Kuhn, his music, and also a live, which Playground was on. And then, uh, I also was on a Steve Swallow recording of Robert Creeley poetry called Home. I don‟t know if you‟ve ever heard that. You would it. It‟s absolutely beautiful poems by Robert Creeley and Swallow‟s music. So I, so I, I recorded with Kuhn on ECM and I recorded with, with Swallow on ECM. Now when, when Kuhn had his first trio that I was involved with, he asked me to be part of the group for some reason. I don‟t know. We were friends but I don‟t, you know, obviously he thought I could add something to it. So it was, uh, Kuhn, Steve Kuhn, Bob Moses, who I love… talk about a genius, man. [laughs]
